_what: Experiment 5: depth map generation. Each matcher makes a depth map of every frame_step'th frame pair of each recording with depth_frames.py (no poses, only a camera depth range), and is scored on points per frame and seconds per frame. To test a new recording or matcher, add it below.

recordings.name: 3DPrintFinal_s30
recordings._depth: Board at about 300-550 mm; the same range as the pose experiment.
recordings._frame_step: 1716 frames: every 25th (69 frames) keeps it the same size as the ice recordings' runs.

recordings.name: ice_pyramid_sun_py2_pass1
recordings._depth: Backlit, tags barely detected, so the board distance is not measured; same range as the shade pass.

recordings.name: ice_pyramid_shade_pyr1_pass4
recordings._depth: Tag 2 measured at 674-839 mm (mean 735); the ice stands in front of the board.

recordings.name: ice_cubes_shade_cub2
recordings._depth: Same range as the pyramid passes for every ice recording (Glen, 17 Oct); the folder name gives ~580 mm.

recordings.name: ice_overhang_shade_hang1
recordings._depth: Same range as the pyramid passes; the folder name gives ~830 mm.

recordings.name: ice_overhang_sun_oh1
recordings._depth: Same range as the pyramid passes. No tag is detected in this pass (checked on 6 frames), so it has no tag-plane accuracy, like the pyramid sun pass.

recordings.name: ice_wave_shade_wave1
recordings._depth: Same range as the pyramid passes; the folder name gives ~720 mm.

_frame_step: Default for recordings that do not set their own.

sgbm_tuned._why: tune_sgbm.py's winner (results/experiments/depth_matchers/sgbm_tuning/tuning.json), tuned against the tag planes on frames this comparison does not use: F1 0.718 -> 0.834, 2.57 -> 0.32 s/frame.

aquastereo._why: Same scale, iterations and left-right check as FoundationStereo, so the learned matchers meet on equal terms.

foundationstereo._why: The fs_s05 settings used for the 3DPrintFinal reconstructions.

figures._why: Depth images of every frame; and for one frame per recording (frame_index into the frames used), the left-right correspondences of a grid of pixels, the same pixels for every matcher.

combined._why: The report figure: the three recordings side by side on one depth scale (250-1400 mm, the union of their ranges).
combined.name: depth_compare_all

crops._why: Close-ups of the objects in the figure frames (box: x0, y0, x1, y1 in the full-size rectified left image, square).
crops.name: depth_crops
crops._common_scale: true: one depth scale and key for all rows; false: a scale per row, fitted to its crop.

figures._extra_crops: More close-up figures like crops, one file each (18 Oct: the four ice recordings added that day). Boxes picked from each recording's depth_compare.jpg, around the ice block (not the tag plate).

extra_crops.name: depth_crops_ice
extra_crops._box: 2x the tight box around each ice block (Glen, 18 Oct), same centre, square, kept inside the 1600x1200 frame; the pyramid's tight box is the one depth_crops uses. Overhang sun left out (Glen).

extra_crops.name: depth_crops_pyramid_sun_shade
extra_crops._box: 1.2x the tight boxes depth_crops uses (Glen, 18 Oct), against the top of the frame, one colour scale.

rows.title: Pyramid, sun
rows._rotate_cw: Turned 90 degrees clockwise to match the shade row's orientation (Glen, 18 Oct).
rows._box: 1.2x box moved right to the frame edge so the pyramid sits higher in the rotated tile (Glen, 18 Oct).
